bib.title: Recursive Introspection: Teaching Language Model Agents How to Self-Improve

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Recursive Introspection: Teaching Language Model Agents How to Self-Improve" (RISE), Yuxiao Qu, Tianjun Zhang, Naman Garg, Aviral Kumar (CMU, UC Berkeley, MultiOn). The PDF carries only "arXiv:2407.18219v2 [cs.LG] 26 Jul 2024", so I treat it as a preprint. It prints no venue.

COVERAGE: All 35 of 35 pages and 105,689 of 105,689 chars were read, including Appendices A-D, pseudocode and hyperparameters. The reference list was skimmed. Figures 1-9 are described only by their captions (no figure extraction run), and the chart values are not in the text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. RISE fine-tunes a single model to revise its own answers over up to 5 turns. Its 5-turn answer (maj@1) beats 5 parallel samples at turn 1 (maj@5) at equal sample count.
 - number: 4% to 8% on GSM8K, 6.5% on MATH (Mistral-7B)
 - setup: GSM8K and MATH, 7B models, no oracle. Majority vote over the candidates from turns 1..j.
 - quote: "Comparing maj@5 performance at the end of 1 turn and 5 turns, we observe a consistent 4% to 8% improvement on GSM8K and an 6.5% improvement on MATH (with Mistral-7B model)."
 - where: p11, 6.1.1
2. 5-turn gains without an oracle (m1@t1 -> m1@t5), Table 1.
 - number: Llama2-7B on GSM8K goes 10.5 -> 11.1 base, then 32.9 -> 39.2 (+6.3) after Boost, 35.6 -> 50.7 (+15.1) at iteration 1 and 37.3 -> 55.0 (+17.7) at iteration 2. Mistral-7B goes 35.3 -> 59.2 (+23.9) on GSM8K and 6.7 -> 18.4 (+11.1) on MATH. Llama2 on MATH: +3.4 at iteration 1, +4.6 at iteration 2.
 - setup: Llama2-7B-chat and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2. Supervision comes from GPT-3.5 samples (best of 5). Only 2 iterations. Eval temperature 1.0.
 - quote: "RISE (“Iteration 1” and “Iteration 2”) boosts up the LLama2 base model’s five-turn performance by 15.1% and 17.7% respectively with each iteration on GSM8K and 3.4% and 4.6% on MATH, w/o any oracle."
 - where: p10, Table 1 and 6.1
3. Prompted self-refine hurts without an oracle, even for GPT-3.5.
 - number: m1@t3 changes on GSM8K are GPT-3.5 -5.4, Mistral-7B -12.5, Eurus-7B-SFT -10.1. With an oracle (p1@t3) the changes are small: +5.2, +4.2, +6.5. Under RISE, GPT-3.5 itself improves only 4.6 over 5 turns.
 - setup: Self-Refine one-shot prompt (Fig 11), GSM8K, 3 turns
 - quote: "Interestingly, we found using prompting-only self-refine [31] largely degrades performance across the board, even with a strong proprietary model, GPT-3.5."
 - where: p10; Table 6 p24 (GPT-3.5: 66.4, 61.0 (-5.4))
4. Imitating the same expert data with single-turn SFT does not produce self-improvement.
 - number: Llama2 on GSM8K, SFT on correct oracle data: m1@t1 27.4 -> m1@t5 34.0 (+6.6). RISE iteration 1 is +15.1.
 - setup: same data RISE collects, trained with plain single-turn SFT
 - quote: "this procedure does not still instill self-improvement capabilities, largely preserving or degrading sequential (“maj@1@turn5”) performance compared to simply sampling one response in the first turn."
 - where: p11
5. Self-distillation (no teacher, best-of-N with N=16 from the learner) gives smaller gains, and only one iteration was run.
 - number: GSM8K, Llama-3-8B 45.3 -> 52.5 (+7.2) base. After iteration 1: 65.6 -> 73.8 (+8.2). Mistral-7B after iteration 1: 36.8 -> 39.5 (+6.6). Text: "by more than 1%" over turn 1.
 - setup: Table 2, no knowledge-boost phase
 - quote: "RISE does not outperform the “m5@t1” performance of the fine-tuned model."
 - where: p11-12. The authors expect it needs more iterations or online RL.
6. Sequential sampling with an oracle checker beats pass@k at turn 1.
 - number: Fig 8 right (no values in the text); Fig 6 shows 5-turn RISE solving problems that pass@B fails for B=5×k.
 - setup: GSM8K, early termination on a correct answer
 - quote: "RISE is able to improve performance more beyond simply sampling more samples at the first turn and computing pass@K, despite this strong assumption of access to an oracle final answer verifier made by the parallel sampling approach."
 - where: p14
7. Error analysis without an oracle: correct-to-incorrect flips fall over turns, unlike the GPT results in Huang et al. [21].
 - number: Fig 10. Default RISE flips fall from 12.3% to 3.9% across turns; the "different correct response" variant falls from 9.8% to 3.3%.
 - setup: Llama2 iteration 1, GSM8K
 - quote: "Both Default RISE and appending a different correct response demonstrate a favorable trend, steadily decreasing from 12.3% to 3.9% and from 9.8% to 3.3%, respectively"
 - where: p22 (Fig 9, p15)
8. Out-of-distribution transfer (Table 3).
 - number: Llama2 base on GSM8K: m1@t1 10.5, m1@t5 11.1. A RISE iteration-1 model trained on MATH reaches 19.3 -> 32.6 (+13.3) on GSM8K. On SVAMP, the model trained on GSM8K goes 42.2 -> 50.0 (+7.8). The model trained on GSM8K and tested on MATH is flat: 4.3 -> 4.4 (+0.1).
 - quote: "RISE Model trained on MATH 19.3 32.6 (+13.3) 48.4 (+29.1)"
 - where: p13
9. Data-composition ablations (Fig 7, 8; Table 4).
 - Multi-turn history with failed attempts beats 1-turn oracle data.
 - Reward-weighted (advantage-centred) training beats filtering to successes only.
 - On-policy, DAgger-style data beats expert-only data.
 - Appending a different correct response after a success gives m1@t5 51.1 (+18.0) vs default 50.7 (+15.1).
 - Repeating the same correct response gives 46.2, which the authors attribute to spurious correlations from duplication.
 - quote: "We find that using all the data leads to improved performance over simply filtering good data" (p14); "repeating a correct response at the end of a successful rollout largely reduces performance." (p22)
10. Weak-to-strong (Table 5, GSM8K).
 - number: Mistral-7B trained on Llama2-7B rollouts reaches m1@t5 62.7 (+24.5), vs 59.2 (+23.9) on its own rollouts. The reverse is worse: Llama2 trained on Mistral rollouts gets 45.2 (+18.1) vs 50.7 (+15.1) on its own, with a lower m1@t1 (27.1 vs 35.6).
 - quote: "training the Llama2 model on Mistral’s mistakes leads to worse performance, likely because errors from the Mistral-7B model are harder to comprehend for a worse base model."
 - where: p23. Caveat: m1@t1 differs between the rows.
11. Comparison with GLoRE (separate models): its 2-turn gain is 3.4% (+SORM, 48.2 -> 51.6), against RISE's 6.3% in two turns. RISE gains 13.4% in 3 turns without an oracle and 23.4% with one (GSM8K, Llama2). GLoRE numbers are taken from its paper, so the comparison is apples-to-oranges.
 - quote: "RISE demonstrates its effectiveness in self-improvement by sequentially enhancing its performance by an impressive 13.4% within just 3 turns without an oracle feedback"
 - where: p26
12. Capacity argument: fitting a sequence of answers gives lower NLL than fitting only the oracle answer. The authors compare this to diffusion vs VAE. This is a hypothesis backed by training-loss curves (256 prompts, 95% CI) in Fig 4-5, with no numbers in the text.
 - where: p7-8
13. Mechanism details.
 - Reward is a sparse binary answer-match.
 - Retry prompt: "The answer is incorrect. Please try again. Here’s the question:<Query>" (Fig 15).
 - Inference has two modes. "With oracle" stops when correct (p1@t5). "Without oracle" runs 5 forced turns and takes a majority vote over all turns so far (m1@t5).
 - Train a "knowledge boosting" SFT stage first.
 - Each iteration restarts from the base model and trains on data from all iterations so far.
 - The context window keeps only the last k turns at iteration k.
 - quote: "starting from the base model but training on data from all iterations thus far is more beneficial than continued fine-tuning from the checkpoint obtained in the previous iteration."
 - where: p6-7

LIMITS
- Authors concede (p16):
 - "we were not able to perform more than two iterations of training with RISE, and no more than one iteration when the supervision comes from the learner itself."
 - Manual iterations are needed, and a more online variant is the likely fix.
 - Fine-tuning is one task at a time.
- Scope: only math (GSM8K, MATH, SVAMP), 7-8B models, a binary answer checker, and training on GSM8K/MATH train splits. No agent or tool tasks, despite the title.
- Weaker or flat cases:
 - Self-distillation does not beat m5@t1.
 - Base Llama2 MATH is tiny (1.9% at turn 1).
 - GSM8K-trained to MATH transfer is about +0.1.
- Not for knowledge-based QA: the authors expect RISE to only encourage hallucination there (p8).
- Supervision comes from GPT-3.5 (best of 5) in the main results, so these are mostly distillation gains, not pure self-improvement. The Self-Refine, GLoRE and V-STaR baselines differ in base model and setup.
- A paper claim ("RISE... attaining an improvement over turns that previous work [21] has not observed in strong proprietary models") is relative to 2023-24 models. Prompted self-correction results are from GPT-3.5 and Llama2 and have dated.
- The Table 6 V-STaR comparison (44.5 vs 35.2 points) mixes iteration counts and sample budgets.

BUILDS ON: Online imitation learning / DAgger (Ross et al. [36]); reward-weighted and advantage-weighted regression (Peters and Schaal [35], Peng et al. [34]); STaR (Zelikman et al. 2022); Self-Refine (Madaan et al. [31]); Huang et al. 2023, "LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning yet" [21]; GLoRE (Havrilla et al. 2024); self-consistency (Wang et al. [51]); V-STaR (Hosseini et al. 2024); Kang et al. 2024 on unfamiliar fine-tuning examples [24]; weak-to-strong generalization (Burns et al. 2023). Reference numbers are as printed. Author names in brackets were not verified against the list except where shown in the read text.

CODE: None. Algorithm 1 (data collection) and Algorithm 2 (inference with a k-turn sliding window then majority vote) are pseudocode on p31.
 - Eq 4.6: max_θ E[ Σ_t log π_θ(ỹ_t|s_t) · exp(r_t/τ) ], with rewards centred per prompt as advantages (p6).
 - Table 7 hyperparameters (p32): 2 epochs, lr 1e-5, cosine schedule, warmup 0.04, 4xA40, batch 1 per device, grad accumulation 16, max length 2048.
 - Table 8 (p32): temperature 1.0 and max_new_tokens 1000 for open models; 0.7 and 512 for GPT.
 - Dataset sizes (p32-33): GSM8K train 7,473 / test 1,319; MATH 7,500 / 1,000; SVAMP 1,000 eval only.

FIGURES (captions only)
- Fig 1 (p2): RISE overview, iterative on-policy training plus majority vote at inference.
- Fig 2 (p4): single-turn problem converted to a multi-turn MDP, and data collection by distillation or self-distillation. It is the quickest explanation of the method.
- Fig 3 (p7): inference with oracle (early stop) vs without oracle (majority vote).
- Fig 6 (p9): fraction of problems that pass@B fails but 5-turn RISE solves.
- Fig 7-8 (p13-14): ablations, and sequential p1@turn k vs parallel pass@k.
- Fig 9 (p15): correct/incorrect transition Venn diagrams over turns.
- Fig 12-14 (p28-30): qualitative cases of small edits, big edits, noise tolerance and error localization.

PROBLEMS
- My first extraction wrote to a fixed shared scratch file, /tmp/papers-t3/loop-2/t.txt. That file was overwritten by another session with an unrelated paper (AlphaEvolve, arXiv:2511.02864). I discarded it. The RISE text used here is in /tmp/papers-t3/loop-2/rise/rise.txt, extracted from the correct PDF (35 pages). Treat anything else in /tmp/papers-t3/loop-2/ as another session's.
- Extraction has dropped spaces in places (for example "Acentralpieceinenabling"), and the Table 1 columns are flattened but legible.
- No embedded instructions were found in the PDF.
- The word-level text "NeurIPS" does not appear, so I cannot confirm a venue from the PDF.
